subject: Literature
title: Irish Mythology and the Ulster Cycle
description: A quick, practical guide to Irish Mythology and the Ulster Cycle.

hook.text: Irish mythology features a warrior so fierce that his body contorts into a monstrous shape during battle frenzy.

buildup.text: Cú Chulainn is the hero of the Ulster Cycle, defending his kingdom single-handedly against an entire army.

discovery.text: The Táin Bó Cúailnge, the central epic, was triggered by a queen's jealousy over a prize bull.

twist.text: Irish monks preserved these pagan stories by writing them down, likely adding Christian commentary as camouflage.

climax.text: Irish mythology was revived during the Celtic Revival and helped fuel the Irish independence movement.

punchline.text: Ancient myths became weapons for modern independence.

quiz.question: How did Irish mythology survive into the modern era?
options: It was continuously performed in public ceremonies
Christian monks wrote down the pagan stories
Roman historians recorded every Irish myth in detail
